answer: An agent economy can resist Sybil attacks with a refundable stake tied to a shared atlas of verified work. Each agent posts a small bond before it can draw nectar from the network. The bond stays locked while peers check the agent's output; honest work returns it, while spam or copied answers forfeit it. A Sybil farm must then fund every fake identity, so a thousand sock puppets cost a thousand bonds. That turns the old fable of free identities into a priced decision: one honest agent is cheap, an army of fakes is ruinously expensive, and the cost scales with the attack, not the defense.
